aya.1: The tea is ready. Sit down and play a few rounds with me?
aya.2: The table feels peaceful today—perfect for thinking things through.
aya.3: Don't rush your discard. I want to see how you build your hand.
aya.4: If you're tired, have some tea first. The table isn't going anywhere.
aya.5: A good hand takes patience, just like tea needs time to steep.
aya.6: I won't go easy on you just because it's you.
aya.7: Your face gives away your whole hand... I'm only teasing.
aya.8: Want to guess which tile I'm hoping to draw?
aya.9: Winning doesn't matter? Say that again after you beat me.
aya.10: One more round. I haven't seen enough of your style yet.

mio.1: ...You're here? Sit. A quiet game sounds good.
mio.2: You don't need to talk. The tiles tell me what you're thinking.
mio.3: Don't discard that one... Never mind. Forget I said anything.
mio.4: You're hesitating too long. The table won't wait.
mio.5: My luck is average today. Good. I'll win with judgment.
mio.6: Don't stare at me. Watch your own tiles.
mio.7: Focus if you want to win. I won't remind you twice.
mio.9: Decide what to discard before you draw. It's faster.

sora.1: Oh, you're here. Let's play a good, clean match.
sora.2: Just so we're clear, I won't hold back. Neither should you.
sora.3: Handle the tiles you draw. Hesitating won't change them.
sora.4: Watch the tiles, not me. My face isn't giving hints.
sora.5: Take your time, but once you decide, commit to it.
sora.6: Best play buys the drinks. Win or lose.
sora.7: Don't tense up. One bad discard—make it back next turn.
sora.8: Come on. Let's play this one straight.
sora.9: Luck changes. Judgment and responsibility don't.
sora.10: Still want to talk? Sure—after this hand.

help.title: Rules & Scoring
help.ruleGoal: Complete five melds and one pair. A concealed hand normally has 16 tiles and 17 after drawing.
help.ruleTurn: Turns proceed counterclockwise. Draw one tile and discard one tile; if no action is taken within 15 seconds, the computer acts for that player.
help.ruleFlowers: A flower is exposed as soon as it is drawn, then a replacement tile is drawn from the wall; flowers are not pre-dealt or replaced in the opening hand.
help.ruleCalls: Chow may only claim the previous player's discard; Pong, Kong and a winning discard may be claimed when available. An exposed Pong may be upgraded to Kong after drawing the fourth tile.
help.ruleReady: Declaring ready locks the hand. Future non-winning draws are discarded automatically.
help.ruleDealer: The dealer keeps the seat after winning or an exhaustive draw, increasing the continuation count without advancing the hand number. After another player wins, the deal passes counterclockwise. The next round starts after all four dealer seats finish, and the match ends only after the North round.
help.ruleWinds: The center display shows the prevailing wind across four East, South, West, and North rounds. The next round begins after all four dealer seats finish; dealer continuations do not advance the hand count. A seat whose fixed wind matches the prevailing wind gains 1 tai for calling Pong or Kong on that wind tile.
help.ruleMatch: The match also ends after settlement if any player reaches zero points. A new match resets all four players to 25,000 points and randomizes the fixed seat winds again.
help.scoringFormula: Payment per opponent = 500 base points + total tai × 200 points.
help.scoringDiscard: Win by discard: only the discarder pays one payment; it is not tripled.
help.scoringSelfDraw: Self-draw: each of the other three players pays the payment.
help.scoringDealer: Dealer involvement adds 1 tai. Each continuation adds another 2 tai (one continuation is 3 dealer tai total); these tai apply only to payments between the dealer and the winner.
help.scoringCoins: After settlement, every {points} table points converts to 1 coin. Funds never fall below zero.
